comes before the Public Service Commission of South Carolina
(Commission) on the Application ofDuke Energy Carolinas, LLC (DEC) and Duke Energy

Companies’ proposed 2026 Request for Proposals for South Carolina-Sited Standalone
Battery Storage (2026 SC Battery RFP or RFP) pursuant to Section
18 of the South
Carolina Energy Security Act (Act 41), including relevant provisions of S.C. Code Ann.
sections 58-42-10 and 58-42-30 (Stage 2 Application).

1 Order), which

general framework for the procurement of South Carolina-sited stand-alone energy storage

resources, including the use of separate utility-owned and third-party-owned procurement

APPLICABLE LAW
Act 41 established a statutory framework for the competitive procurement of stand-
alone energy storage resources to be located in South Carolina. §§ S.C. Code Ann. 58-42-

10, 58-42-30 (Supp. 2025). Sections 58-42-10 and 58-42-30 set forth specific standards for
the Commission’s review of the Companies’ Stage 2 Application.
Section 58-42-10 provides that it is in the public interest for electrical utilities to
competitively procure certain stand-alone storage additions to be located in South Carolina,
consistent with the utilities’
2023 Integrated Resource Plans (IRP) approved by the
Commission
or subsequent Commission-approved
annual
IRP updates,
with
such
resources intended to be in service by January 1, 2035. S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-10(A).
Electrical utilities must procure stand-alone storage resources through at least a
biennial competitive procurement process consistent with the requirements of S.C. Code
Ann. section 58-42-30. S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-10(B). The target procurement volume for
stand-alone energy storage may not exceed the portion of stand-alone storage in the most
recent Commission-approved IRP or annual IRP update that is equal to the portion of the
respective electrical utility’s peak load attributable to South Carolina customers. S.C. Code
Ann. § 58-42-30(A)(2).! The procurement of stand-alone energy storage facilities must
result in a reasonable balance of electrical utility ownership and independent third-party
ownership, as determined by the Commission. S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-30(A)(4)(a).
Act 41 permits utility participation in the competitive procurement, subject to
certain protections. Specifically, “{a]n electrical utility and its affiliates may offer proposals
into the competitive procurement provided that appropriate safeguards are in place to
' Stand-alone energy storage facilities with a design capacity less than or equal to twenty megawatts and
intended primarily to address local reliability improvements or local capacity constraints are not subject to
the competitive procurement requirements of this section. S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-30(A)(3).

ensure that such proposals do not receive any advantage in the bid evaluation process.”
S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-30(A)(4)(b).
Act 41 also requires cost-effectiveness confirmation prior to final procurement
awards. The electrical utility must “confirm that the resources selected are cost-effective
using methodologies and current inputs reflected in the applicable integrated resource plan
or integrated resource plan update approved by the commission for that electrical utility[,]”
prior to making final awards. S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-10(G). Section 58-42-30 also
provides that stand-alone storage facilities shall be subject to operational protocols,
equipment specifications, and inspections established by the electrical utility that are
necessary to ensure the reliability of the electrical utility system and requires information
regarding such resources to be provided to the Office of Regulatory Staff(ORS). S.C. Code
Ann. § 58-42-30(B).
Regarding cost recovery, Act 41 provides that electrical utility costs associated with
facilities owned by an independent third-party power producer shall be capitalized and
included within the electrical utility’s rate base for ratemaking purposes. S.C. Code Ann.
§ 58-42-30(A)(4)(b). Act 41 further provides that electrical utilities may recover costs
incurred through the competitive procurement of stand-alone energy storage through rates
established pursuant to S.C. Code Ann. § 58-27-870. S.C. Code Ann. § 58-42-30(C). S.C.
Code Ann. section 58-27-870 governs general rate proceedings before the Commission and
requires Commission approval of proposed rates.
In addition, S.C. Code Ann. section 58-37-40(C)(4) provides that the review and
acceptance of an IRP by the Commission, or the inclusion of any specific resource in an
accepted IRP, is not determinative of the reasonableness or prudence of the acquisition or

construction of any resource or the making of any expenditure. Ultimately, the electrical
utility retains the burden to show that its investments and expenditures are reasonable and
